text:
Alex K.: Heads-up: RFC follow-up — thinking about splitting the LoadableShard surface into two pieces: a minimal Loader (sync/async read) and a BackpressureCoordinator that owns prefetch budget + warmup scheduling. Want quick takes before I open a PR.

Maria T.: Curious — what's the main driver? Is it to make warmup policy pluggable or to reduce coupling in the runtime?

Alex K.: Both. We keep bumping into cases where per-model warmup heuristics need more signals (request priority, model variant, tenant SLO). If the loader also decides backpressure it ends up duplicating logic or leaking runtime internals.

Jin L.: Agree with separation. API suggestion: keep Loader as pure IO semantics and add a Backpressure trait that exposes `request_capacity()` + `on_eviction()` callbacks. Pseudocode:```go
// Loader: simple reads, no scheduling
type Loader interface {
  ReadShard(shardID string, offset int64, len int) ([]byte, error)
}

// Backpressure coordinator: gives tokens for warmup and accepts hints
type BackpressureCoordinator interface {
  RequestTokens(ctx context.Context, hint PrefetchHint) (tokens int, delay time.Duration)
  ReleaseTokens(n int)
  OnEvict(shardID string)
}
```

Samir: That looks clean. A few tradeoffs:
- We add one extra IPC/edge call per prefetch decision (though it can be in-process).
- Backwards compat: existing loaders expect to be able to block and take IO decisions. We need a compat shim.

Maria T.: Important to specify semantics for `delay` vs synchronous denial. If coordinator returns a delay, loader should schedule async prefetch; if zero tokens and zero delay maybe treat as rejected. Also how to handle partial fills (e.g., tokens < requested).

Jin L.: Implementation sketch: default coordinator runs local policy (burst tokens per device, global per-host budget, tenant fairness). For dedicated deployments we can swap to a deterministic preallocator for throughput guarantees. This decoupling lets us test policies in isolation and A/B them.

Alex K.: Telemetry requirements: we need counters for `prefetch_requested`, `prefetch_granted`, `prefetch_delayed_ms`, `evictions_during_warmup`. Samir — can you add those to the roadmap?

Samir: Yep. Also want a gauge for `pending_prefetch_bytes` and histogram for `prefetch_latency` (split by hot vs cold path). Those will be essential for tuning token bucket sizes.

Maria T.: Migration plan idea: add a coordinator default that wraps existing behavior (returns tokens instantly) so no change to current loader callers. Then opt-in per-model via model manifest flag `warmup.coordinator=v2`. Gradual rollout.

Jin L.: One gotcha: some legacy loaders assume synchronous blocking ReadShard and rely on side effects. We should document a `BlockingReadShard` adapter that will synchronously request tokens and block the caller thread while keeping core Loader primitives async.

Alex K.: Good point. I'll include a blocking adapter in the PR. Also plan to add unit tests that simulate eviction races (prefetch granted -> eviction before load) and assert coordinator `OnEvict` semantics.

ops-bot: ci/build-status: flaky on linux-integration (test_prefetch_race) — FYI, not related to this thread but might affect PR merge.

Samir: Noted — we'll rerun CI after PR. For perf, let's capture a simple benchmark: baseline (current combined impl) vs split with no-op coordinator vs split with tokenized coordinator under 4 workloads: low qps, high qps small seq, high qps long seq, bursty startup.

Alex K.: Plan: I'll open RFC PR with API diffs, a compat shim, telemetry plan, and benchmark harness. If folks can comment on the API sketch above and any missing signals (e.g., per-request priority, variant hint), that helps.

Maria T.: +1 on separating concerns. Suggest adding `prefetch_priority int` in PrefetchHint; higher numbers == higher urgency.

Jin L.: Also add `is_fallback bool` in hint so coordinator deprioritizes fallback warmups.

Alex K.: Great — will incorporate those. Thanks everyone, will tag reviewers when PR is ready. :thumbsup:
